핵심이슈.summary:
## 오늘의 한국 경제 흐름 요약

오늘 한국 경제는 **성장과 물가 사이의 긴장**, 그리고 **고용 부진**이 맞물리는 복합적인 국면을 보였다. KDI는 올해 성장률 전망을 1.9%에서 2.5%로 상향 조정하며 낙관적 신호를 보냈지만, 동시에 물가 전망도 2.7%로 높이고 한국은행에 금리 인상 가능성을 열어둘 것을 권고해 **성장 회복이 인플레이션 압력과 함께 온다**는 점을 분명히 했다. 미국에서도 예측시장이 연간 인플레이션 5% 가능성을 거론하고, 노동시장 약화 신호가 동시에 감지되는 등 글로벌 스태그플레이션 우려가 국내 통화정책 불확실성을 높이고 있다. 한편 4월 취업자 증가 폭이 7만 4천 명으로 16개월 만에 최저를 기록하며 고용률마저 하락 전환해 경기 체감은 여전히 냉랭하지만, 정부는 추경 집행 본격화를 통해 5월 이후 개선을 기대하고 있다. MMF·예금 유입으로 통화량(M2)이 늘고, 채권시장은 금리 인상 가능성에 부담을 받는 가운데, 환율은 하반기 점진적 안정이 전망되나 변동성 관리가 관건으로 꼽혔다.

key_headlines.title: KDI Significantly Raises 2026 Growth Forecast to 2.5% from 1.9%
key_headlines.summary: The Korea Development Institute upgraded its economic growth outlook for 2026 to 2.5%, citing strong semiconductor exports driven by AI demand as offsetting Middle East-related inflation risks. The institute also recommended rate increases to manage inflation expectations.

key_headlines.title: April Employment Growth Lowest in 16 Months at 74,000
key_headlines.summary: South Korea added only 74,000 jobs in April, marking the weakest employment growth in 16 months, with employment rates showing a downward reversal signaling labor market softening.

key_headlines.title: US Prediction Markets Signal Potential 5% Inflation This Year
key_headlines.summary: Prediction markets are indicating that US inflation could reach 5% in 2026, reflecting growing concerns about persistent inflationary pressures globally.

key_headlines.title: Citibank Forecasts 4 Rate Hikes, Raising Growth Outlook to 3.0%
key_headlines.summary: Citibank raised South Korea's 2026 growth forecast to 3.0% and projects four interest rate increases by April 2027, bringing the benchmark rate to 3.5%.

key_headlines.title: M2 Money Supply Expands as MMF and Deposit Inflows Accelerate
key_headlines.summary: March M2 money supply growth accelerated 0.4% month-over-month as increased flows into money market funds and bank deposits expanded the monetary base.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economic prospects have brightened significantly with the Korea Development Institute raising its 2026 growth forecast to 2.5% from 1.9%, primarily driven by booming semiconductor exports fueled by AI demand. However, this optimistic outlook is tempered by inflationary pressures, particularly from rising international oil prices and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Inflation expectations are climbing, with price pressures expected to reach 2.7%, prompting policy authorities to consider interest rate hikes. The labor market shows signs of weakness with April employment growth hitting a 16-month low of 74,000 new jobs, indicating economic softening despite positive growth forecasts.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Korea Development Institute has recommended that the Bank of Korea raise its benchmark interest rate above normal levels while exercising restraint on fiscal stimulus to prevent economic overheating. Citibank forecasts four rate increases totaling 150 basis points by April 2027, bringing the policy rate to 3.5%, with 2026 growth now estimated at 3.0% and 2027 at 2.8%. Rising inflation expectations, driven by global commodity prices and Middle East tensions, are creating urgency for monetary tightening despite potential growth concerns. The KDI specifically noted that expected inflation levels are rising, necessitating flexible monetary policy responses from the central bank.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korean equities are performing strongly, with the KOSPI attempting to break through 7,900 as semiconductor-led gains drive market sentiment. A record number of ETFs with net assets exceeding 1 trillion won have emerged, with international equity funds gaining particular traction as market liquidity concentrates in equities. Global bond markets are experiencing significant volatility, with Japanese 10-year yields hitting 29-year highs near 2.6%, while British gilt yields reached 28-year highs amid political uncertainty over PM Starmer's leadership. The yen has weakened significantly to around 157.75 per dollar, reflecting currency market pressures.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korean semiconductor and battery industries are attracting intense strategic attention as companies navigate US-China technology competition and global supply chain realignment. Japan's SoftBank is entering the battery manufacturing sector using former Sharp facilities to address AI data center power demands and tap growing energy storage markets. South Korea is emphasizing semiconductor and battery production as survival strategies in the technology-dominated global economy, with the Korean Academy of Engineering holding forums to discuss technology sovereignty risks and trade responses. Silver demand surged dramatically in the first quarter, jumping 20-fold year-over-year as semiconductor and advanced industry applications drive industrial metal consumption.
sections.Real Estate: South Korea's May apartment sales outlook improved dramatically, with the Housing Industry Research Institute's index rising 19.1 points to 80.0, driven by rising jeonse (long-term lease) prices that are stimulating home purchase demand. Jeonse price increases are creating a virtuous cycle encouraging apartment purchases despite elevated house prices. However, rental housing supply is contracting as the government permits tax-resident single-home owners to sell properties, while multi-home owners tighten supply strategically, threatening tenant housing security. Illegal jeonse contract trading has surfaced as rising property values incentivize broker-mediated schemes, with recent arrests highlighting increased criminal activity in the housing market.
sections.International Economy: US inflation reached its highest level in three years in April, complicating Federal Reserve policy decisions and pushing rate cut expectations further into 2027 or beyond. Following the Trump-Xi meeting, US liquefied natural gas exports to China have resumed for the first time in over a year, marking a potential thaw in trade tensions between the two powers. The Fed is preparing for leadership transition as Bart Barsh advances to Fed chair, set to navigate competing pressures between inflation control and the Trump administration's rate-cut expectations starting next month's FOMC meeting. Global uncertainty from Middle East conflicts is pressuring inflation worldwide, while political instability in the UK is destabilizing bond markets.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korean companies and government are actively pursuing AI infrastructure investment strategies, with UAE's major investors attending Seoul forums to explore semiconductor and AI infrastructure partnerships despite Middle East geopolitical tensions. Walmart is cutting approximately 1,000 headquarters positions as it accelerates AI investments, reflecting a broader corporate trend of reorganizing for AI-driven efficiency. NH Agricultural Financial Group has launched comprehensive AI governance frameworks as regulatory requirements tighten following South Korea's January 2026 AI Basic Law implementation. The Korean Exchange is integrating AI capabilities acquired through the FairLabs acquisition into capital market operations, while AI GPU rental price futures markets are expected to emerge as computing capacity becomes a critical resource comparable to oil.
sections.Others: Duoback recorded double-digit sales growth of 15.5% year-over-year in Q1 2026, reaching 626 billion won as the gaming chair manufacturer expands into Northern European markets including Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and Estonia. The Korea Exchange is implementing AI tools for core capital market operations following its acquisition of FairLabs. An AI GPU rental pricing futures market is anticipated to launch, establishing computing capacity as a critical 21st-century commodity. Various investment forums and conferences, including the Korea Investment Week (KIW) 2026 at the Shilla Hotel, are showcasing opportunities in AI and Korean cultural content investment strategies.
